plan: Store the input dict as a deep copy in the Workspace constructor and return deep copies from to_data(), so external mutation can never alias internal state.
Provide a single recursive depth-first generator over the item tree; total_word_count() and unresolved_markers() are folds over that generator.

Use two compiled regexes: one matching marker tokens [[?identifier]] (stripped from note text and mined for identifiers), and \b\w+\b for counting the remaining words; references contribute their declared word_count and their unresolved list.
Render outline() by seeding the lines with the workspace title, then recursing with an explicit depth counter, indenting two spaces per nesting level and formatting each line as '<kind>: <title>'.

Implement move() as validate-then-mutate: locate the item and destination (resolving the literal 'workspace' to the root list), check container kind, check the destination is not the moved item or inside its subtree via identity walk, and range-check the index — all before touching any list; only then pop and insert, guaranteeing failed moves leave to_data() unchanged.
Detect illegal containment with an identity-based subtree membership check (is comparisons), which is immune to structurally equal but distinct items.
mechanisms: deep-copy isolation at construction and export
recursive depth-first generator as the single traversal primitive
compiled regex pair for marker stripping and word tokenization
validate-then-mutate move protocol (all ValueErrors raised before any mutation)
identity-based subtree containment check for self/descendant move rejection
parent-list + index location records for O(1) removal and insertion
